articles.title: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages
articles.summary: Over the last week or so, we have seen a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage that brought entire companies to a standstill, and a banking outage at JPMorgan Chase. But the consensus is that there are more to come.
body: Microsoft and the US government agree there are more outages to come.

“The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.”
Microsoft President Brad Smith issued a similar warning about further outages on CBS News’ Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan, but sounded a much more ominous tone.

“I think we have to be prepared, frankly, for the coming months because this isn’t the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks … The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now.”

articles.title: Kodak’s next collectible is a tiny digital photo frame that doubles as a tracker
articles.summary: After expanding its Charmera collection with a Millennium Edition featuring Y2K-inspired designs earlier this year, Reto's follow-up to its tiny Kodak camera is an equally small digital photo frame you can use to display your shots.
body: You can personalize the SlideTag with a photo slideshow, message, or QR code transferred from your phone over Bluetooth.

The Kodak SlideTag will be available for $34.99 each and, like the Charmera, will feature a series of retro designs distributed in mystery boxes so you don’t know which one you’re going to get. Kodak also sells a complete set of all eight vintage designs for $279.92 if you don’t like mysteries; however, there’s a ninth “secret edition” only available in the individual boxes with a sleek metallic finish.

For those who grew up in an era where projectors are small enough to integrate into phones, the SlideTag is designed to look like a modernized version of the film slides that were used to project photos decades ago. Instead of film, the SlideTag features a 1.54-inch color E Ink screen that mixes six colored inks to display photos at a resolution of 240 x 240.

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
articles.summary: John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips. Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang ’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the most…
body: The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was put at risk by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.
Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO on 12 November after allegations surfaced of extramarital relationships with the suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, had been executive director of Megaspeed International. Megaspeed facilitated about $12bn in chip sales, in violation of export controls in the US, where the Trump administration has prohibited the selling of advanced AI chips to China.
On Sunday’s edition of CNN’s State of the Union, the Trump administration’s national intelligence director, Jay Clayton, said he suspected China was able to obtain Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips.

articles.title: I covered myself in sleep trackers to find the very best
articles.summary: Get a better night’s sleep with monitoring and guidance from smartwatches, smart rings, smart bands and sleep earbuds. The best sleep masks and best Bluetooth sleep masks. Getting quality sleep is just as crucial as getting enough sleep. And how you feel in the morning only tells part of the story.
body: Armed with this information, you can learn how your lifestyle affects your sleep. Maybe your after dinner cappuccino triggers a night of tossing and turning, or you’re more restful after evening workouts. As the wise GI Joe once said, knowing is half the battle. And the more you know about your sleep, the better chance you have of improving it.

As a consumer technology journalist for more than two decades, I began wearing fitness trackers in the early 2010s and have since reviewed hundreds of products in the sleep and fitness space. After spending more than 15 years tracking my sleep nightly, I have a deep understanding of how wearables work, which brands and products are reliable and how to best interpret app data.

I wore up to five wearables at a time (two wrist devices, two rings, and earbuds) for at least seven nights each. Every morning, I plotted sleep data into a spreadsheet, including duration, sleep stages (light, REM, deep, awake), along with average sleep heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV) when available.

articles.title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds
articles.summary: Transparency International says Queensland’s David Crisafulli was ‘by far the most frequently accessed’ state leader, with 13 meetings. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: Bosses at 10 datacentre companies secured almost 120 meetings with premiers and ministers in five states over a three-year period, with experts declaring this is “just the tip of the iceberg”.

Analysis by Transparency International Australia argues these meetings, when combined with political donations, demonstrate “unfettered access” to decision-makers that creates an “uneven playing field”.

The report found donations from major datacentre companies and their contracted lobbying firms nearly tripled over the past three years from $685,000 to $1.8m, coinciding with increased investment across Australia.

The analysis found the Queensland leader, David Crisafulli, was “by far the most frequently accessed state premier”, with public diaries showing he has met datacentre executives 13 times in the past three years.

articles.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
articles.summary: Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve 19th-century Riemann hypothesis. A mathematician at Anthropic has said that the San Francisco -based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in…
body: Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
On Saturday afternoon, two organizations announced that they had independently verified Alpöge’s claim after reviewing the programming language he used to share the solution.

The proof evidently marks another breakthrough in the use of AI for complicated math problems – even as mathematicians express uneasiness around extremely lucrative private companies dishing out millions of dollars for the technology to solve problems.

“Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line,” Alpöge wrote, while anthropomorphizing the AI software. “No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

articles.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
articles.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land.
body: The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access.

With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses.

The biggest effects, however, occurred when reduced calorie intake was combined with a shift toward healthier diets. In this scenario, up to 7 million deaths could be avoided each year by 2050, while around 46 million hectares of agricultural land would have become available for other uses. This suggests that alongside weight-loss medicines, we need to make healthier options more widely available, affordable, and more appealing.
points: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them.

articles.title: Here's how much Starlink cost in 2020 vs. 2026
articles.summary: Throw in discounts and fluctuating rates, and two customers could end up paying vastly different bills for the same Starlink satellite service.
body: Starlink's cheapest home plan costs $44 less per month than it did in 2020, but hardware ownership and regional pricing have changed.

Starlink rolled out its public beta in October 2020, with the equipment costing $499 and the monthly subscription $99. Six years down the road, SpaceX's satellite internet service starts at $55 monthly for US customers, with equipment rentals available at no upfront cost in select areas. That's $44 less a month, or $528 less annually, on the subscription cost alone.

The company also jacked up its residential rates in 2026, but the entry-level rate is still lower than it was in 2020. Throw in discounts and fluctuating rates based on local demand, and two customers could end up paying vastly different bills for the same satellite internet service.

SpaceX's first public beta was rolled out as the "Better Than Nothing Beta." True to its very transparent (and accurate) name, customers were asked to expect download speeds of 50 to 150 Mbps and latency of 20 to 40ms, paired with occasional periods of zero connectivity.
points: Throw in discounts and fluctuating rates, and two customers could end up paying vastly different bills for the same Starlink satellite service.
